question: How much of the AI buildout is debt the balance sheets do not show yet, and who carries it if a tenant walks away?

call.stance: The risk off the books is still rising.
call.line: Leases pile up faster than they start, Alphabet's backstops cost more to carry, and Oracle's cash leans on its customers' prepayments.
actions: Add the five 'not yet commenced' lines in February 2027: $1,118.5 billion at mid-2026 against Moody's $662 billion at end-2025.
Read guarantees at their threshold, not booked liability: Meta's Hyperion guarantee of about $28 billion carried none on June 30, 2026.
Strip prepayments from Oracle's operating cash on Dec 14: $11.4 billion of $23.1 billion in the quarter to Aug 31, 2026.
flips: The five 'not yet commenced' lines at Dec 31, 2026 sum to no more than the $1,118.5 billion of mid-2026.
Alphabet's annual report puts its backstops' liability at 1.86% of notional or less at Dec 31, 2026, where it stood at June 30.
Oracle's Dec 14 release puts customer prepayments at 40% or less of six-month operating cash.

nextTest.event: Oracle's second quarter: whether customer prepayments with a financing component pass 40% of operating cash for the six months to November 30, from 49.2% in the quarter to August 31, 2026.

resolver.rule: Divide the line for the increase in deferred revenues from customer prepayments with significant financing component by net cash provided by operating activities, both for the six months ended November 30, 2026, as printed in the statement of cash flows of the earnings release, or of the Form 10-Q when the release does not print the six months. The answer is yes if the line is above 40% of operating cash flow, which includes any case where operating cash flow is zero or negative; no if it is 40% or less. In the quarter to August 31, 2026 the same two lines gave $11,363 million of $23,103 million, 49.2%.
resolver.question: For the six months ended November 30, 2026, does Oracle's increase in deferred revenues from customer prepayments with significant financing component exceed 40% of its net cash provided by operating activities?

source.label: SEC EDGAR, Oracle second-quarter fiscal 2027 results (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-Q, statements of cash flows (CIK 1341439)

resolver.ambiguity: If neither the earnings release nor the Form 10-Q prints both lines for the six months by January 11, 2027, or the prepayment line is renamed, merged or dropped, the test is inconclusive, and the Result says what was read and what was missing; the next reading is January 18, 2027, in the Form 10-Q's statement of cash flows.

think.baseRate: In the quarter to August 31, 2026, customer prepayments with a financing component were $11.4 billion of Oracle's $23.1 billion of operating cash, or 49.2%.
think.outsideView: For the six months to reach 40% or less, the second quarter's share would have to fall to about 31% on similar operating cash, which an ordinary collections quarter could do.
think.wouldChange: Fewer new data center contracts paid in advance, or a quarter of strong ordinary collections, would lower the number, and a drop in operating cash would raise it.

notes.label: Everyone agrees
notes.text: The commitments are signed. The voices split on whether they are debt now, and on who holds them if a tenant walks.

notes.label: The thread
notes.text: Part 3 said the debt might fail before the machines; Part 11 read Meta's guarantee as a signal. Part 17 counts what is signed.

settles.event: The year-end filings: whether the leases not yet begun at the five pass $1.2 trillion as printed at December 31, 2026, from $1,118.5 billion in mid-2026.
Alphabet's annual report: whether the liability on its data center credit derivatives passes 1.86% of notional at December 31, 2026, its level at June 30, 2026.
Oracle's second quarter: whether customer prepayments with a financing component pass 40% of operating cash for the six months to November 30, from 49.2% in the quarter to August 31, 2026.
Meta's annual report for 2026: whether it consolidates Hyperion or records a liability above zero for its residual value guarantees, neither at June 30, 2026.

lead.name: Michael Burry
lead.line: Lenders would not hold the residual value risk of Meta's Louisiana venture without protection, so Meta guaranteed up to $28 billion of it, a sign that the parties closest to the asset doubt its value will hold.

lead.name: Michael Burry
lead.line: A purpose-built data center has no deep resale or sublease market, unlike an office, so capacity nobody needs gets written down, as Meta's 2022 charges on offices and data centers showed.

lead.name: Scott Galloway
lead.line: Investors are paying too little attention to the obligations off the balance sheet that sit under Big Tech's AI infrastructure spending.

against.name: Haim Zaltzman
against.line: Guarantees and credit support are probably what it takes to clear deals of this size at this speed, as wrappers and insurance do for car and aircraft finance.
against.why: This side reads the guarantee as debt kept off the books. Zaltzman reads the same tool as the price of financing a deal this large at all.

lead.name: Harley Bassman
lead.line: Most hyperscalers own cash businesses that can cover the cost of their borrowing; short of a breakup, the debt gets repaid even if shareholders suffer.

lead.name: Harris Associates Oakmark
lead.line: Oakmark holds bonds of Meta, Alphabet, Amazon and Oracle for their wider spreads and lower leverage than the broader investment-grade market.

lead.name: Gaetano
lead.line: What matters for the hyperscalers is how much earnings growth each dollar of capital buys, not the year capital spending peaks.

against.name: Michael Burry
against.line: Lenders would not hold the residual value risk of Meta's Louisiana venture without a guarantee from Meta of up to $28 billion.
against.why: This side trusts the tenants' cash. Burry's point is that the lenders closest to the campus would not take its residual value without Meta standing behind it.

lead.name: Kris
lead.line: Oracle sent a force majeure notice on Project Jupiter, its New Mexico campus tied to Stargate, and Kris hopes it will not prove the first crack.

lead.name: Kakashii
lead.line: Unlike Amazon, Google and Microsoft, which paid for their data centers from strong free cash flow, Oracle entered the AI era already carrying tens of billions of dollars of debt.

lead.name: Jeremie Eliahou Ontiveros
lead.line: AI labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic are not investment grade and cannot afford the upfront spending a data center takes, which limits how far they can build for themselves.

against.name: Harley Bassman
against.line: The hyperscalers, not the labs, do the borrowing, so a lab's failure would be an equity problem rather than a bond problem; the hyperscalers have the cash to pay their debt.
against.why: This side follows the loss to the weakest tenant. Bassman answers that the borrowers are the hyperscalers, whose cash keeps a lab's failure out of the bond market.

expansions.expansion: Residual value guarantee, a promise to pay the shortfall if a leased building is worth less than an agreed amount when the lease ends.
Variable interest entity, a vehicle a company may control without owning a majority, which decides whether it must consolidate it.
National Association of Insurance Commissioners, the body of state insurance regulators that reviews the ratings insurers rely on.
